ærlighed.explanation: "Ærlighed" means "honesty". It is the noun for the adjective "ærlig" (honest): "Han er ærlig" (He is honest).

ærter.explanation: "En ært" means "a pea". In Denmark, "gule ærter" (yellow peas) is also the name of a traditional soup. To say you are having that soup, say "Vi skal have gule ærter i aften" (We are having pea soup tonight).

at bade.explanation: "At bade" means "to bathe / swim". When you go into the sea or a lake, say "Vi bader i havet" (We swim in the sea). Do not mix it up with "at svømme" (to swim): "Hun svømmer hver morgen" (She swims every morning).

at bagatellisere.explanation: "At bagatellisere" means "to downplay". It comes from "en bagatel" (a trifle). To say it is wrong to treat something serious as small, say "Man må ikke bagatellisere vold" (You must not downplay violence).

at bage.explanation: "At bage" means "to bake". To say what you bake, put the thing after the verb: "Vi bager brød i weekenden" (We bake bread at the weekend).

at bakke op.explanation: "At bakke op" means "to back up / support". When you say which person or decision you support, put "om" (about) after "op": "Vi bakker op om hendes forslag" (We back up her proposal).

at balancere.explanation: "At balancere" means "to balance". When you find the right mix between two things, say "Hun balancerer arbejde og familie" (She balances work and family).

at bande.explanation: "At bande" means "to swear (curse)". Do not mix it up with "at sværge" (to swear a promise): "Jeg sværger, at jeg siger sandheden" (I swear that I am telling the truth).

at banke på.explanation: "At banke på" means "to knock". When you knock on something, "på" (on) must follow the verb: "Han banker på døren" (He knocks on the door). Without "på", "at banke" is also used for a heart: "Hjertet banker" (The heart pounds).

at barbere sig.explanation: "At barbere sig" means "to shave". It is built from "at barbere" (to shave) and "sig" (yourself). When you talk about "he", "sig" stays as it is: "Han barberer sig hver morgen" (He shaves every morning). To shave someone else, leave "sig" out: "Jeg barberer ham" (I shave him).

at bearbejde.explanation: "At bearbejde" means "to process / work on". It is built from "at arbejde" (to work). When you deal with something hard in your feelings, say "Hun bearbejder sin sorg" (She is processing her grief).

at bebo.explanation: "At bebo" means "to inhabit". It is built from "at bo" (to live). "At bo" needs "i" (in) before the place: "Familien bor i huset" (The family lives in the house). "At bebo" takes the place directly: "Familien bebor huset" (The family inhabits the house).

at bebrejde.explanation: "At bebrejde" means "to blame". When you blame yourself, say "Jeg bebrejder mig selv" (I blame myself). To name the mistake you blame the person for, add "for" (for): "Hun bebrejder ham for fejlen" (She blames him for the mistake).

at bede.explanation: "At bede" means "to ask / pray". When you ask someone to do something, say "Jeg bad hende om at komme" (I asked her to come). When you pray, say "Hun beder til Gud" (She prays to God). Do not mix it up with "at spørge" (to ask a question): "Jeg spørger ham, hvad klokken er" (I ask him what time it is).

at bede om.explanation: "At bede om" means "to ask for". It is built from "at bede" (to ask / pray) and "om" (for). When you ask politely for something in a café, say "Må jeg bede om regningen?" (May I ask for the bill?). Do not mix it up with "at spørge" (to ask a question): "Jeg spørger om vejen" (I ask about the way).

at bedrage.explanation: "At bedrage" means "to deceive". When someone is unfaithful to a partner, it means "to cheat on": "Han bedrog hende" (He cheated on her).

at bedømme.explanation: "At bedømme" means "to judge / assess". It is built from "at dømme" (to sentence). When you ask someone to assess a danger, say "Kan du bedømme risikoen?" (Can you assess the risk?). Do not mix it up with "at dømme" (to sentence), which is the word used in court: "Retten dømmer manden til fængsel" (The court sentences the man to prison).

at befinde sig.explanation: "At befinde sig" means "to be (located)". When you say where people are, "sig" changes to match them: "Vi befinder os i Aarhus" (We are in Aarhus). Do not mix it up with "at være" (to be): "Hvor er du?" (Where are you?)

at befri.explanation: "At befri" means "to free / liberate". It is built from "fri" (free). When you free someone from a worry, add "for" (from) before the worry: "Pengene befrier ham for bekymringer" (The money frees him from worries).

at begejstre.explanation: "At begejstre" means "to thrill / excite". When something makes people enthusiastic, that thing is the subject: "Filmen begejstrer børnene" (The film thrills the children). Do not mix it up with "spændt" (excited, eager), which says how you yourself feel: "Jeg er spændt på resultatet" (I am excited about the result).

at begrave.explanation: "At begrave" means "to bury". When you drop an idea for good, say "De begravede planen" (They buried the plan).

at begrunde.explanation: "At begrunde" means "to justify". It is built from "en grund" (a reason). When someone asks you to back up an answer, say "Kan du begrunde dit svar?" (Can you justify your answer?)

at begrænse.explanation: "At begrænse" means "to limit". It is built from "en grænse" (a border). When you limit yourself, add "sig" (yourself): "Jeg begrænser mig til én kop kaffe" (I limit myself to one cup of coffee).

at begunstige.explanation: "At begunstige" means "to favor". It is built from "en gunst" (a favor). When a rule helps one group more than another, say "Loven begunstiger store firmaer" (The law favors big companies).

at begynde.explanation: "At begynde" means "to begin". To say what you begin to do, add "at" (to) and a verb: "Jeg begynder at læse" (I begin to read). To say when something starts, use it alone: "Kurset begynder i januar" (The course begins in January).

at begynde på.explanation: "At begynde på" means "to begin on". When you start a job, say "Han begynder på et nyt arbejde i morgen" (He begins a new job tomorrow). When a verb follows, use "at begynde" without "på": "Jeg begynder at læse" (I begin to read).

at begå.explanation: "At begå" means "to commit (a crime)". It also goes with mistakes. To say someone made a mistake, say "Han begik en fejl" (He made a mistake). With "sig" (yourself) it has a different meaning, "to get by": "Hun kan begå sig på fransk" (She can get by in French).

at behandle.explanation: "At behandle" means "to treat". When you talk about how someone acts toward a person, say "Han behandler mig godt" (He treats me well). When an office deals with a case, it means "to handle": "Kommunen behandler sagen" (The city is handling the case).

at beherske.explanation: "At beherske" means "to master / control". It is built from "at herske" (to rule). When you keep your feelings under control, add "sig" (oneself): "Han kunne ikke beherske sig" (He could not control himself).

at beholde.explanation: "At beholde" means "to keep". It is built from "at holde" (to hold). When you keep a promise, use "at holde" and not "at beholde": "Jeg holder mit løfte" (I keep my promise).

at behøve.explanation: "At behøve" means "to need". To ask whether something has to be done, say "Behøver jeg at skrive under?" (Do I need to sign?) A very common phrase for needing a thing is "at have brug for" (to need): "Jeg har brug for hjælp" (I need help).

at bekende.explanation: "At bekende" means "to confess". When you openly stand by a belief, add "sig til" (yourself to): "Hun bekender sig til sine værdier" (She stands by her values).

at bekræfte.explanation: "At bekræfte" means "to confirm". When a result shows that a guess was right, say "Testen bekræfter vores mistanke" (The test confirms our suspicion).

at bekymre sig.explanation: "At bekymre sig" means "to worry". To say who you worry about, add "om" (about): "Jeg bekymrer mig om dig" (I worry about you). When you say "you", "sig" becomes "dig": "Du bekymrer dig for meget" (You worry too much).

at bekæmpe.explanation: "At bekæmpe" means "to fight / combat". It is built from "at kæmpe" (to struggle). When you work against a harmful thing, say "Vi bekæmper fattigdom" (We fight poverty). Do not mix it up with "at slås" (to brawl): "Drengene slås i skolegården" (The boys are brawling in the schoolyard).

at belaste.explanation: "At belaste" means "to burden / strain". It is built from "en last" (a load). When something harms a thing, say "Kørsel belaster miljøet" (Driving burdens the environment). When you put your problems on a person, say "Jeg vil ikke belaste dig med mine problemer" (I do not want to burden you with my problems).

at belyse.explanation: "At belyse" means "to shed light on". It is built from "lys" (light). Literally, it means "to light up". When a lamp lights a place, say "Projektøren belyser scenen" (The spotlight lights up the stage).

at belære.explanation: "At belære" means "to lecture (someone)". To say what you lecture someone about, add "om" (about): "Han belærer mig om penge" (He lectures me about money). To tell someone to stop, say "Du skal ikke belære mig" (Do not lecture me).

at belønne.explanation: "At belønne" means "to reward". It is built from "en løn" (a wage). To say what the reward is for, add "for" (for): "Hun blev belønnet for sin indsats" (She was rewarded for her effort).

at bemærke.explanation: "At bemærke" means "to notice / remark". When you say something in passing, it means "to remark": "Hun bemærkede, at det var koldt" (She remarked that it was cold). To make people pay attention, say "Bemærk!" (Note!)

at benytte.explanation: "At benytte" means "to use". It is built from "nytte" (use). When you take advantage of something, add "sig af" (yourself of): "Jeg benytter mig af tilbuddet" (I am taking advantage of the offer).

at benægte.explanation: "At benægte" means "to deny". When you reject an accusation, say "Han benægter anklagen" (He denies the accusation). Do not mix it up with "at nægte" (to refuse): "De nægter ham adgang" (They refuse him entry).

at beordre.explanation: "At beordre" means "to order (command)". When someone with authority sends people somewhere, say "Chefen beordrede os hjem" (The boss ordered us home). When you order food, use "at bestille" (to order): "Vi bestiller to pizzaer" (We order two pizzas).

at beregne.explanation: "At beregne" means "to calculate". It is built from "at regne" (to do sums). To say how a price is worked out, say "Prisen beregnes ud fra vægten" (The price is calculated from the weight).

at berette.explanation: "At berette" means "to report / tell". It is the verb for "en beretning" (an account): "Vi læste hans beretning om krigen" (We read his account of the war).

at berige.explanation: "At berige" means "to enrich". It is built from "rig" (rich). When something brings money to a country, say "Olien har beriget landet" (The oil has enriched the country).

at berolige.explanation: "At berolige" means "to calm / reassure". It is built from "rolig" (calm). When news puts your mind at rest, say "Det beroliger mig" (That reassures me). When a doctor gives a drug that calms, the drug is "et beroligende middel" (a sedative).

at berøre.explanation: "At berøre" means "to touch / affect". When a matter involves many people, say "Sagen berører mange" (The matter affects many people). When something moves you emotionally, say "Jeg blev dybt berørt" (I was deeply moved).

at besejre.explanation: "At besejre" means "to defeat". It is built from "en sejr" (a victory). When you overcome a fear, say "Hun besejrede sin angst" (She overcame her fear).

at besidde.explanation: "At besidde" means "to possess". When someone owns something valuable, say "Hun besidder en stor formue" (She possesses a large fortune). Do not mix it up with "at have" (to have): "Jeg har en cykel" (I have a bike).

at beskadige.explanation: "At beskadige" means "to damage". It is built from "en skade" (damage). When you describe something that is already damaged, use "beskadiget" (damaged): "en beskadiget bil" (a damaged car).

at beskatte.explanation: "At beskatte" means "to tax". It is built from "en skat" (a tax). The same word "skat" also means "treasure": "De fandt en skat" (They found a treasure).

at beskrive.explanation: "At beskrive" means "to describe". It is built from "at skrive" (to write), but it does not need paper. To say what you describe something as, add "som" (as): "Han beskriver hende som venlig" (He describes her as friendly).

at beskylde.explanation: "At beskylde" means "to accuse". It is built from "en skyld" (guilt). To name the charge, add "for" (of): "Hun blev beskyldt for at lyve" (She was accused of lying).

at beskytte.explanation: "At beskytte" means "to protect". When people protect themselves, add "sig" (themselves): "Cyklister beskytter sig med en hjelm" (Cyclists protect themselves with a helmet).

at beskæftige sig med.explanation: "At beskæftige sig med" means "to deal with / work with". When you ask someone what they do, say "Hvad beskæftiger du dig med?" (What do you do?) Without "sig" and "med", "at beskæftige" means "to employ": "Firmaet beskæftiger 50 personer" (The company employs 50 people).

at beslaglægge.explanation: "At beslaglægge" means "to confiscate". When the police take away a car, say "Politiet beslaglagde bilen" (The police seized the car).

at beslutte.explanation: "At beslutte" means "to decide". To name what you decided to do, add "at" (to) before the verb: "Vi besluttede at blive hjemme" (We decided to stay home). With "mig" (myself) it means "to make up your mind": "Jeg har besluttet mig" (I have made up my mind).

at beslutte sig.explanation: "At beslutte sig" means "to decide". To name the choice you made, add "for" (for) after "sig" (oneself): "Jeg besluttede mig for at blive" (I decided to stay). Without "sig", "at beslutte" is followed by "at" (to) and a verb: "Vi besluttede at flytte" (We decided to move).

at bestemme.explanation: "At bestemme" means "to decide". When you ask who is in charge, say "Hvem bestemmer her?" (Who is in charge here?) To say who has control over someone, add "over" (over): "Du bestemmer ikke over mig" (You do not tell me what to do).

at bestemme sig.explanation: "At bestemme sig" means "to make up one's mind". To tell someone to choose now, say "Bestem dig!" (Make up your mind!) Without "sig", "at bestemme" is for the person in charge: "Chefen bestemmer" (The boss decides).

at bestige.explanation: "At bestige" means "to climb (a mountain)". When a king or queen takes the throne, it means "to ascend": "Hun bestiger tronen" (She ascends the throne). For a tree, use "at klatre" (to climb): "Drengen klatrer i et træ" (The boy climbs a tree).

at bestille.explanation: "At bestille" means "to order". When you reserve a table, it means "to book": "Vi har bestilt et bord til otte" (We have booked a table for eight).

at bestille tid.explanation: "At bestille tid" means "to make an appointment". Literally, it means "to book time": "at bestille" (to book) and "tid" (time). To name the person you will see, add "hos" (at, with): "Hun bestiller tid hos tandlægen" (She makes an appointment with the dentist).

at bestride.explanation: "At bestride" means "to dispute". When a company or a person covers the costs, it means "to cover": "Firmaet bestrider udgifterne" (The company covers the costs).

at bestræbe sig.explanation: "At bestræbe sig" means "to strive". It is built from "at stræbe" (to aspire). To say what you strive to do, add "på at" (to) before the verb. When you say "we", "sig" becomes "os": "Vi bestræber os på at svare hurtigt" (We strive to answer quickly).

at bestå.explanation: "At bestå" means "to pass (an exam) / consist". When you say what something is made of, add "af" (of): "Holdet består af ti spillere" (The team consists of ten players).

at besvare.explanation: "At besvare" means "to answer". It is built from "at svare" (to answer). "At svare" needs "på" (on): "Han svarer på brevet" (He answers the letter). "At besvare" takes no "på": "Han besvarer brevet" (He answers the letter).

at besvime.explanation: "At besvime" means "to faint". To say someone has fainted, use "er" (is), not "har" (has): "Hun er besvimet" (She has fainted).

at besøge.explanation: "At besøge" means "to visit". To ask whether you can come for a visit, use "at komme på besøg" (to come for a visit): "Må jeg komme på besøg?" (May I come for a visit?)

at betale.explanation: "At betale" means "to pay". When you pay a bill, no small word follows: "Jeg betaler regningen" (I pay the bill). To pay someone back, add "tilbage" (back): "Jeg betaler dig tilbage i morgen" (I will pay you back tomorrow).

at betale af.explanation: "At betale af" means "to pay off". It is built from "at betale" (to pay) and "af" (off). To ask how much someone pays toward a loan each month, say "Hvor meget betaler du af hver måned?" (How much do you pay off each month?)

at betale for.explanation: "At betale for" means "to pay for". To cover another person's share, put the person after "for": "Jeg betaler for dig" (I am paying for you).

at betale med kort.explanation: "At betale med kort" means "to pay by card". To ask a shop whether you can pay by card, say "Kan jeg betale med kort?" (Can I pay by card?) To pay in cash, say "at betale kontant" (to pay in cash): "Jeg betaler kontant" (I pay in cash).

at betale sig.explanation: "At betale sig" means "to pay off (be worth it)". To say what is worth doing, use "det" (it) and add "at" and a verb: "Det betaler sig at lære dansk" (It pays off to learn Danish). Do not mix it up with "at betale" (to pay money): "Jeg betaler regningen" (I pay the bill).

at betale tilbage.explanation: "At betale tilbage" means "to pay back". When you say what money you pay back, put it before "tilbage": "Jeg betaler pengene tilbage" (I pay the money back). To name the person who gets the money, put the person straight after "betale": "Jeg betaler dig tilbage" (I pay you back).

at betegne.explanation: "At betegne" means "to denote / describe". When you say what a word stands for, say "Ordet 'bil' betegner et køretøj" (The word 'bil' stands for a vehicle).

at betjene.explanation: "At betjene" means "to serve / operate". When someone works a machine, say "Han betjener kranen" (He operates the crane). When a waiter brings food to a table, use "at servere" (to serve): "Tjeneren serverer maden" (The waiter serves the food).

at betragte.explanation: "At betragte" means "to regard / consider". When you look at something calmly for a while, it means "to watch": "Hun betragter solnedgangen" (She watches the sunset).

at betro.explanation: "At betro" means "to confide". To confide in someone, add "sig" (yourself) and "til" (to): "Hun betroede sig til sin søster" (She confided in her sister). When you hand something important to a person you trust, it means "to entrust": "Jeg betror ham nøglerne" (I entrust him with the keys).

at betvivle.explanation: "At betvivle" means "to question / doubt". It is built from "at tvivle" (to doubt). No small word follows it: "Jeg betvivler hans ord" (I doubt his word). "At tvivle" needs "på" (on) instead: "Jeg tvivler på hans ord" (I doubt his word).

at betyde.explanation: "At betyde" means "to mean". When something is important to you, say "Det betyder meget for mig" (It means a lot to me). When you explain what follows from something, say "Det betyder, at vi må vente" (That means that we must wait).

at beundre.explanation: "At beundre" means "to admire". When you look at something beautiful with delight, say "Vi beundrer udsigten" (We admire the view). Do not mix it up with "at kunne lide" (to like): "Jeg kan lide min nabo" (I like my neighbor).

at bevare.explanation: "At bevare" means "to preserve / keep". To say you stay calm, use "at bevare roen" (to keep calm): "Han bevarer roen" (He keeps calm). To keep a thing you own, use "at beholde" (to keep): "Jeg beholder bogen" (I keep the book).

at bevilge.explanation: "At bevilge" means "to grant". To say that money has been granted, say "Der er bevilget to millioner kroner" (Two million kroner have been granted).

at bevise.explanation: "At bevise" means "to prove". When you show that something is true, say "Hun beviste, at det var sandt" (She proved that it was true). When you show what you can do, use "at bevise sit værd" (to prove your worth): "Han ville bevise sit værd" (He wanted to prove his worth).

at bevæge.explanation: "At bevæge" means "to move". To move yourself, add "sig" (yourself): "Han bevæger sig langsomt" (He moves slowly). To move house, use "at flytte" (to move): "Vi flytter til Odense" (We are moving to Odense).

at bevæge sig.explanation: "At bevæge sig" means "to move". When you move your own body, say "Han bevæger sig langsomt" (He moves slowly). To carry a thing to another place, use "at flytte" (to move): "Jeg flytter bordet" (I am moving the table).

at bide.explanation: "At bide" means "to bite". When an insect bites you, say "Myggen bed mig" (The mosquito bit me). To bite into food, add "i" (in): "Hun bider i æblet" (She bites into the apple). Do not mix it up with "at bede" (to ask / pray), which looks similar: "Jeg beder om hjælp" (I ask for help).

at bidrage.explanation: "At bidrage" means "to contribute". To say what you give to, add "til" (to): "Hun bidrager til forskningen" (She contributes to the research).

at binde.explanation: "At binde" means "to tie / bind". When you tie hair up, add "op" (up): "Jeg binder håret op" (I tie my hair up).

at binde snørebånd.explanation: "At binde snørebånd" means "to tie shoelaces". It is built from "at binde" (to tie) and "snørebånd" (shoelaces). To tie a scarf, use the same verb: "Jeg binder et tørklæde" (I tie a scarf).

at bistå.explanation: "At bistå" means "to assist". It is the verb for "en bistand" (assistance). To say who gets the help, put the person after the verb: "Revisoren bistår firmaet" (The accountant assists the company).

at blaffe.explanation: "At blaffe" means "to hitchhike". To ask for a ride, say "Må jeg få en lift?" (Can I get a ride?)

at blande.explanation: "At blande" means "to mix". To mix two things together, add "med" (with): "Han blander mælk med kaffe" (He mixes milk with coffee). Do not mix it up with "at blande sig" (to interfere): "Bland dig ikke i det" (Stay out of it).

at blande sig.explanation: "At blande sig" means "to interfere". To say what you interfere in, add "i" (in): "Du skal ikke blande dig i andres liv" (You should not interfere in other people's lives). Without "sig" (yourself), "at blande" means "to mix": "Jeg blander saft og vand" (I mix cordial and water).

at blegne.explanation: "At blegne" means "to fade". It is built from "bleg" (pale). When a face turns white, it means "to go pale": "Hun blegnede af skræk" (She went pale with fear).

at blinke.explanation: "At blinke" means "to blink / wink". When stars or lights shine on and off, say "Stjernerne blinker" (The stars are twinkling). When a driver signals a turn, say "Han blinker til venstre" (He signals left).

at blive.explanation: "At blive" means "to become / stay". When something changes, say "Det bliver koldt i aften" (It will get cold tonight). When you do not leave, say "Jeg bliver hjemme" (I stay at home). When you say what will happen, say "Det bliver godt" (It will be good). Do not mix it up with "at være" (to be): "Han er læge" (He is a doctor).
